name: Lakeside Trading, Sheds & Outdoor Furniture
about:
Lakeside Trading LLC has operated from Narragansett, Rhode Island since 1999, when founder Dave Harrigan liquidated his 401(k) and life savings to purchase a trailer load of hand-made clay chimineas from Mexico. The family-owned business began wholesaling those chimineas to local garden centers and selling at seasonal markets before expanding into outdoor structures.

Today the company procures, installs, and services American-made sheds, greenhouses, chicken coops, gazebos, garages, pergolas, playsets, and pavilions from a 5,000-square-foot showroom and display yard A staff of 20 full-time employees — some with more than 15 years’ tenure — handles custom design, site preparation, delivery, and installation, completing over 1,000 structure installations and selling more than 2,000 pieces of furniture annually.

Lakeside serves residential customers throughout Rhode Island, offering both stock and customizable options. Its outdoor furniture line features marine-grade hardware and recycled plastic poly lumber backed by a 20-year workmanship warranty, while Amish-crafted structures carry a 10-year warranty and a lifetime service guarantee. The company also provides shed relocation, foundation preparation, and free on-site consultations.

Harrigan’s original leap of faith established a culture of fair pricing and personal service that remains the company’s stated differentiator: a locally rooted, family-run operation that stands behind every product it sells.

name: Lance Industries
old_description: Since 1985, Lance Industries has manufactured high-quality commercial meat marinators and vacuum meat tumblers. You can find Lance Industries’ equipment across the globe in meat markets, grocery stores, butcher shops, delis, restaurants, and meat processing facilities.
about:
Lance Industries was founded in 1985 in Hartford, Wisconsin, where it began producing vacuum massage tumblers with design input from Family Farms Meats and the engineering staff at LMI Manufacturing. The company introduced the first American-made meat tumbler, built specifically for the needs of the U.S. meat industry.

The company manufactures four models of commercial vacuum meat tumblers — the LT-5 (50 lb capacity), LT-15 (200 lb), LT-30 (500 lb), and LT-60 (1,000 lb) — featuring variable-speed drives, digital timers, built-in vacuum systems, and wheels on all units for mobility through standard 32-inch doors. Drums are constructed from thicker-gauge steel, and each unit includes a removable lid with a metal-detectable gasket for cleaning and food safety. More than 3,000 tumblers have been installed worldwide.

Lance equipment serves meat markets, grocery stores, butcher shops, delis, restaurants, meat processors, and meat-alternative processors. Customers cited in company materials include Haun's Meat & Sausage, Bardini's Country Smokehouse, Bob's Processing, Hudson Meats, and Quality Cut Meats, which reported a used tumbler still operating after 34 years.

Lance Industries emphasizes durability, reliability, and U.S.-based technical support with a fully stocked repair department. The company is a member of the American Association of Meat Processors (AAMP) and the Wisconsin Association of Meat Processors (WAMP), exhibiting at both national and state conventions to stay close to customer needs.

about:
Landmark Packaging Inc. was founded in 2012 in Aurora, Colorado, by Mark, Paul, and Jeff. The trio set out to serve small and medium-sized businesses in the Rocky Mountain region with custom packaging solutions at affordable prices.

The company operates as both a manufacturer and distributor of packaging materials, offering boxes, bags, labels, janitorial supplies, and personal protective equipment. Its 48,000-square-foot warehouse supports digital printing, custom box and label production, container fabrication, and fulfillment services such as labeling, polyethylene bagging, stretch film, shrink wrap, tape, and bubble wrap.

Landmark focuses on Colorado-based small and medium enterprises across various sectors, providing stock and custom packaging for shipping, storage, and retail needs. Customers include local manufacturers, distributors, and service businesses that require flexible, cost-effective packaging.

The founders’ original vision — maintaining a focus on smaller businesses while expanding capabilities — remains the company’s guiding principle. Landmark emphasizes affordable pricing, custom digital printing, and a growing range of packaging options to help its clients succeed.

name: Lang's Old Car Parts, Inc.
old_description: Lang's Old Car Parts is a family owned company with a true passion for the Model T Ford. We have the most complete catalog available on the market, including new and used Model T parts. We also carry a large selection of accessories, books and instructional movies. Ever since our founding over 35 years ago, we have worked hard to provide the best Model T parts with the great customer service and free technical support.
about:
Lang's Old Car Parts, Inc. operates from Baldwinville, Massachusetts, where it was founded more than 35 years ago as a family-owned business built around a passion for the Model T Ford. The company began with family members selling used parts at swap meets before expanding into a dedicated catalog and online operation.

The firm specializes in supplying new, used, and new-old-stock (NOS) parts for the Model T, along with accessories, books, and instructional videos. Its catalog covers hundreds of categories — from engine and transmission components to body, upholstery, and electrical items — and also includes parts for Fordson tractors. The company does not manufacture parts; it sources and stocks inventory for direct sale to customers via phone and an e-commerce site.

Primary customers are Model T owners, restorers, and hobbyists, as well as Fordson tractor enthusiasts. The staff, three-quarters of whom own a Model T themselves, provide free technical support to help buyers identify the correct components for their projects.

The company emphasizes its comprehensive catalog, knowledgeable staff, and free technical assistance as key differentiators, aiming to be the go-to resource for Model T restoration.

We are the premier manufacturing and service facility for Truck Mounted Equipment, Fire Equipment, Truck Tanks and Tank Trailers when the requirements call for absolute off-road dependability.
about:
Largo Tank & Equipment Inc. operates from Farmington, New Mexico, where it has served the Southwest for over 25 years. The company was founded as a manufacturing and service facility focused on truck-mounted equipment, fire apparatus, and tank trailers built for off-road dependability. No founders or ownership details are disclosed.

At its Farmington facility, Largo designs, welds, and assembles custom truck bodies, cargo tanks, and fire equipment. The shop produces flatbeds, welder bodies, platform and dump bodies, service bodies, oilfield and chemical treater trucks, crane bodies, contractor beds, propane service trucks, and van bodies. It also stocks thousands of hard-to-find parts and represents hundreds of brands, offering same-day shipping on stocked items and 24/7 emergency service.

The company serves oil and gas, propane, construction, fuel delivery, mining, crane service, delivery, fire and emergency, government, farm and ranch, plumbing, and landscaping sectors. Customers include municipal fleets, public works departments, wildland firefighting units, and commercial contractors operating in the San Juan Basin and surrounding regions.

Largo emphasizes custom design and close collaboration to meet unique project requirements, aiming to make customers' work easier and build equipment right every time. Its "Built Largo Tough" philosophy reflects a focus on reliability in harsh off-road conditions.

name: Larson Cable Trailers, Inc
old_description: Founded in 2000 by Rick Larson, Larson Cable Trailers revolutionized the industry as the original creator of the patented cable fiber installation trailer.
about:
Larson Cable Trailers, Inc. is based in Huron, South Dakota. Founded in 2000 by Rick Larson, the company began as an offshoot of his underground utilities business, Larson Digging Inc. Unable to find a trailer that could lift cable reels, “figure 8,” and rewind cable efficiently, Larson built his own patented cable fiber installation trailer. In early 2024, the business was acquired by Felling Trailers and continues to operate as a separate division.

The company manufactures patented cable fiber installation trailers designed to handle reel lifting, figure‑8 layout, and rewinding in a single unit. Its product line includes the original Larson Cable Trailer and, since 2024, the Drive Trailers series. The division also runs an online parts store supplying trailer components, manuals, and warranty service.

Primary customers are public and private contractors, rural telephone cooperatives, electric cooperatives, and city municipalities involved in fiber‑optic and power infrastructure projects. The trailers are used for burying cable, fiber‑optic installation, and electrical line construction across the United States.

The business was started to solve a real‑world problem Larson faced daily: the need for a versatile, durable trailer that could increase crew efficiency. The patented design aims to let crews lay more cable in less time by combining multiple functions into one piece of equipment.

name: Latest Metalworks
old_description: ISO 9001-Certified Metal Fabrication with Over 20 Years of Large-Scale Program Experience
about:
Latest Metalworks operates from Murrieta, California, in Riverside County. Founded nearly two decades ago, the company has built a reputation for large-scale metal fabrication across Southern California and nationally. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides full-program fabrication from engineering review through final delivery. Core processes include laser cutting with an AMADA fiberoptic laser, waterjet cutting on an OMAX machine, forming and bending via an Amada press brake, 8-axis tube bending and rolling, and LADBS-certified welding. Additional capabilities cover engineering and CAD using Solidworks, secondary finishing, and a dedicated packaging department for kitted shipments. The facility handles production runs, structural assemblies, exhibit structures, prototype programs, and architectural metalwork.

Clients span automotive OEM, industrial, architectural, EV and solar, and R&D sectors. Notable references include Temeka Group for retail, museum, and commercial projects; the City of Oceanside Water Department for plant maintenance fabrication; Inokinetic for product manufacturing; Tube Bending Technology, an aerospace supplier; and V&T Tooling Inc. for tooling components.

The company emphasizes blending traditional craftsmanship with advanced technology to turn client visions into reality. Its ISO 9001:2015 certification (#1120219) and LADBS structural steel fabricator approval (#FB03359) underscore a commitment to quality management and code compliance.

name: Laurel Wire Company, Inc.
old_description: Since 1983, Laurel Wire has worked with a wide array of industries and manufacturers to deliver quality parts on time to meet customer specs. Our humble beginnings as a small
about:
Laurel Wire Company, Inc. was founded in 1983 in Plainville, Connecticut, by Dick Clark and his business partner William Killiany. At just 27 years old, Clark started the business in his garage on Laurel Street with a focus on wire straightening and cutting services.

The company specializes in precision wire straightening and cutting for round and strip materials, handling diameters from 0.030 to 0.364 inches and lengths up to 40 feet depending on alloy and temper. It also provides through-feed centerless grinding services. Laurel Wire purchases all raw material and processes it to customer specifications, serving both prototype and large-scale production needs.

Its customer base spans automotive, aerospace, industrial, and consumer sectors. Components produced by Laurel Wire are used in heat exchangers, jewelry, springs, fishing lures, tubing mandrels, acoustical ceilings, pipe organs, bookbinding, extension drills, hinges, wire forms, heating elements, and Swiss screw machining applications.

Clark founded the company on a passionate commitment to the customer, a principle that remains central. The firm emphasizes customizable material, length, size, and temper options, proactive communication throughout projects, and a quality-first approach that it says distinguishes it from competitors.
